CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules (workflow, r-package, ci, native-code, correctness, assurance) come from the r-skills plugin’s rules/, loaded at session start because of the marker above. Never copy them here. Where this file and a shared rule disagree, this file wins for this package. Cloud sessions do not load the plugin and run without them.

What this is

zuslothdb is to SlothDB what duckdb is to DuckDB: the engine’s C++20 source vendored into the package and compiled at install, with a DBI driver on top, so that SQL over local CSV, Parquet, JSON and Arrow IPC files works with no system library, no server and no download. Runtime dependencies are DBI and methods only. It is deliberately not a duckdb replacement (upstream calls itself experimental), not a network client (HTTP, S3, extension loading and the ask module are compiled out), and not a dplyr backend of its own in v0.1.0.

.agents/design.md is the specification and outranks this file; it records the RFC it came from. Its §5.1 fixes the rule for the API: the shape is duckdb’s, the scope is upstream’s Python binding’s. Its §12 decisions and §14 open questions are the maintainer’s to settle; do not settle one in code without recording it there.

Current state

Scaffolded 2026-11-17 with create-pkg.sh; no functionality yet, and DESCRIPTION still has the scaffold’s placeholder title, description and author. Nothing of the engine has been built with any compiler. The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0. Its Stage 1 is a go/no-go spike (decision D1): the package may stop there.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #1 for v0.1.0. Sibling packages that depend on this one before CRAN does: none.

Commands

Only the shared commands so far. The design plans tools/vendor.R, which copies the pinned upstream commit, applies the patches and writes the source list into src/Makevars.

Architecture

To be written as stages land; see .agents/design.md §4 for the three planned layers (vendored C++, sdb_ glue C++, R DBI classes). The scaffold set up a C stub, src/zuslothdb.c, through use_c(); the design needs C++20 (CXX_STD = CXX20), so Stage 1 replaces it.

Invariants that are easy to break

None is enforced by code yet. The design already fixes these:

  • No C++ exception crosses into R, and no R API call that can longjmp runs while a SlothDB object with a destructor is live on the stack (§4.3). Breaking either leaks or crashes the session.
  • The shared library exports only R_init_zuslothdb. SlothDB carries a duckdb_fastpforlib namespace copied from DuckDB, so visible symbols clash when duckdb is loaded in the same session.
  • Nothing vendored is edited by hand: every change to upstream is a patch recorded in tools/vendor.yaml with its reason (§4.2).
  • Offline only (D4), and no file written outside tempdir() and the user’s dbdir.
  • Two threads unless the user sets threads (D5).
  • A 64-bit integer that does not fit a double is a zuslothdb_type_error, never a silent rounding (§6).

Testing

None yet: no conformance suite, helpers or measured runtime. The design’s §10 plans DuckDB as the oracle (in a separate development project, not in Suggests), DBItest, upstream’s doctest suite on the patched tree, and hostile inputs under the sanitizers, with ZUZUSLOTHDB_SKIP_HEAVY and ZUZUSLOTHDB_SLOW_TESTS as the switches.

Continuous integration

R-CMD-check.yaml and coverage.yaml call the shared pedrobtz/r-actions workflows (r-cmd-check.yml@v1, coverage.yml@v1). pkgdown.yaml is the r-lib example workflow, building the site to gh-pages. The roadmap marks Stages 1, 2, 3 and 6 full, besides the three closing stages.

Vendored native code

Planned, not yet vendored: SlothDB (MIT) at commit 8180f215847015944c935f56f008d194e2c1494c, with its own third_party/ subset (zstd decompressor, snappy, fastpforlib, miniz, unordered_dense.h). Licences and the initial patch list are in the design’s front matter and §4.2. Fill in the vendored paths, the patch count and the update procedure when Stage 1 vendors it.
